Oct 20 : Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November. The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said. The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could not immediately determine the scale of the cuts. Qualcomm did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September.

One of the world's biggest smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets. Its shares have risen just 1.5 per cent in 2026, compared with gains of more than 12 per cent for the benchmark S&P 500 and nearly 60 per cent for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index. In its latest earnings report in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-center and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. The company expects the majority of its chip sales to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as it expands into the fast-growing AI data-center market. Amon said in the memo business priorities, organizational needs, skills and expertise would be considered in making the cuts. "As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require," he wrote. "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed."

Source: Reuters

Oct 20 : Hasbro raised annual revenue forecast on Tuesday, betting on strong demand for its digital games, including "Magic: The Gathering", ahead of the crucial holiday season. The Play-Doh maker has posted consecutive gains in its digital gaming segment over the past seven quarters, while an increase in sales of collectibles linked to Marvel, K-Pop Demon Hunters and Transformers have boosted demand for traditional toys. Revenue in its Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment rose 31 per cent during the third quarter, while consumer products segment was up 4 per cent from a year ago. The company's shares were up 1 per cent in premarket trading. The toymaker expects fiscal 2026 revenue to grow in the range of 7 per cent to 9 per cent on constant currency basis, compared with its prior forecast a 5 per cent to 7 per cent rise.

BERLIN, Oct 20 : Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) said on Tuesday that it was investigating the online publication of emails stolen by unknown hackers during a cyberattack last month. An AfD spokesperson said hackers had targeted a hosting service provider used by the party and apparently copied data from a small number of email accounts, most of which had not been used for years.  "The recent online publication of what is presumably a portion of this data is currently being investigated," the spokesperson said. "A preliminary assessment can only be provided once this investigation has been concluded." The spokesperson did not say how much data was stolen.

The statement followed a report by Bild newspaper saying over 420,000 emails linked to the party had been published online.  According to Bild, the material included emails sent by party figures such as co-leader Alice Weidel as well as bank statements, academic certificates and membership lists. The website hosting the material was offline by Tuesday afternoon, but archived versions showed a trove of 281 gigabytes of data under the headline "The party's own records, unedited". The leak comes as the AfD, which has topped national opinion polls and made gains in recent state elections, faces calls from some politicians and civil society groups for it to be banned.  They argue the party threatens Germany's democratic constitutional order, an accusation the AfD rejects as politically motivated.

FAST

LONDON, Oct 20 : Britain's competition regulator said on Tuesday it was seeking to loosen Apple's grip on contactless payments by proposing that the company lower fees and remove technical barriers, helping rival services compete with Apple Pay. The Competition and Markets Authority said its proposals would result in "substantially lower access fees" and easier access to Apple's contactless technology, opening the market to competition from digital banks and other providers. The proposed measures are less onerous than those imposed by the European Union in 2024, which included giving third-party wallet developers free access. Since then, companies including Vipps, PayPal, Klarna, Curve and BBVA have launched alternative payment apps, the CMA said. CMA Chief Executive Sarah Cardell said the proposals would open the door to more innovation and more choice, as well as boosting Britain's important fintech sector.

"We have heard that high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions relating to Apple's contactless technology make it too difficult for challengers to innovate and compete," she said.   "By removing barriers to entry, we can help create the conditions for brilliant British businesses with great ideas to develop new products and services here - from payment apps and digital IDs to travel passes and digital keys." The CMA is consulting on the proposals until November 17, before making a final decision. Contactless payments have grown rapidly in popularity, accounting for 39 per cent of all payments, compared with just 3 per cent a decade ago, the CMA said. More than 60 per cent of adults use a digital wallet, with Apple Wallet the most popular in Britain, it added. Apple said it had already made it possible for developers to offer contactless payments in their apps through NFC, which allows an iPhone to talk to a payments terminal or reader, and through its secure element, which stores sensitive material such as card credentials and cryptographic keys. The company said this allowed developers to create products and services, including in-store payments, transit passes and event tickets, while ensuring users' sensitive data remained protected by the highest security standards. "We do not believe the CMA should require Apple to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections," an Apple spokesperson said. "We will continue to engage constructively to reach an outcome that is in the best interest of our users."

Source: Reuters

FAST

MILAN, Oct 20 : Smart glasses that resemble ordinary eyewear are under increased scrutiny from European regulators and advocacy groups, leaving investors questioning whether sales can keep booming as Ray-Ban maker EssilorLuxottica reports third-quarter results. EssilorLuxottica launched its Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, capable of filming and recording, in 2023 and the market has grown rapidly. Global shipments of AI-enabled glasses jumped to 8.4 million units in 2025 from around 2.1 million in 2024, according to research group Omdia. EssilorLuxottica's Meta eyewear accounted for 81.3 per cent of global shipments in the first half of this year. When it releases its third-quarter results on Tuesday, EssilorLuxottica is not expected to give precise data on the value of smart glasses sales, but may provide an indication. In its second-quarter trading update, it said smart glasses sales nearly doubled compared to the same period a year earlier.

SOME GOVERNMENTS CONSIDER BANS The resemblance to ordinary eyewear has been a factor in the success of EssilorLuxottica's Meta smart glasses, and is in contrast to Google Glass more than a decade ago, whose bulky, futuristic design limited mainstream consumer appeal. But the design's discretion is troubling to regulators. Last week, the European Data Protection Board, or EDPB, which brings together national privacy regulators, said the devices facilitated covert recording, including of bystanders' conversations. Louis Larere, portfolio manager at French asset manager BDL, echoed that concern. "The fact that smart glasses include a camera, allow users to livestream and instantly share content on social media could become a problem," he said. So far Norway has taken the toughest stance among governments, saying earlier this month it planned a temporary ban on the use of AI glasses in selected locations. Australia said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces. In a preliminary, non-binding statement, the EDPB urged manufacturers to combine measures such as visible recording lights, sound alerts and notifications to nearby devices while recording. The authority also suggested limiting live streaming, automatically blurring bystanders' faces and using location-based technical restrictions in sensitive settings like hospitals or schools. PRIVACY CONCERNS MAY LIMIT ADOPTION Ross Gerber, CEO of California-based wealth management firm Gerber Kawasaki, which holds Meta shares, said privacy concerns and social stigma could limit wider adoption even though smart glasses still hold long-term potential. "People will make you feel uncomfortable if you wear them, and people feel uncomfortable wearing them because of this," he said, adding that his pair of Meta glasses was sitting unused in his garage. A Meta spokesperson said the glasses remain popular for music, calls and live translations. "They were built to be noticed which is why every pair with a camera has a bright light on the front that flashes when you take a photo or video you can share with others," they added. "It's important that rules protect people's rights while supporting innovation and consistency across technologies," an EssilorLuxottica spokesperson told Reuters, adding that the company is working to help consumers understand how to use the glasses responsibly and respectfully. Data regulators in Italy and Austria both told Reuters that they were investigating incidents involving smart glasses being used by pupils in schools, and France's data watchdog previously said it had received a small number of complaints. "Authorities should think about banning these devices in public spaces in a more coordinated manner," Kleanthi Sardeli, a lawyer at European digital rights advocacy group NOYB, told Reuters. Growing privacy concerns could pose a challenge for EssilorLuxottica and Meta as they seek to position AI glasses, which can be used for making calls and listening to music, as a potential future alternative to smartphones. "(Privacy concerns) are a risk to this category. We already saw something similar more than a decade ago with Google Glasses," Cedric Rossi, luxury and consumer goods equity research analyst at Stifel, said. Rossi said Meta's unveiling in September of camera-free audio glasses was a first step toward addressing regulatory and privacy concerns. However, he added that, without a camera, users cannot fully benefit from the AI capabilities the devices are designed to offer. Other companies, meanwhile, are still drawn to the category and Google, in partnership with Samsung, plans to release its Gemini AI glasses before the end of this year. Apple is also expected to release its own smart glasses. BofA analysts in a report this month assessed the regulatory risk as limited and that an outright ban was unlikely even if additional restrictions emerge, particularly in Europe.

Source: Reuters

China's Finance Minister Lan Foan called on APEC members to work more closely together to boost growth at a time when the global economy has been rocked by rapid change and the fallout from geopolitical conflicts.

HONG KONG: The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum has an increasingly important role in helping the world economy tackle the challenges it faces, China's Finance Minister Lan Foan said on Tuesday (Oct 20). "APEC, as an engine of global economic growth, shoulders greater responsibility," Lan said in remarks at the opening of the APEC Finance Ministers' meeting in Hong Kong. He called on the 21 members of the Pacific Rim grouping, which includes the United States, Japan and Russia, to work more closely together to boost growth at a time when the global economy has been rocked by rapid change and the fallout from geopolitical conflicts. Lan also urged governments to cooperate on AI, the digital economy and green sector development, saying these efforts would create new sources of growth. China, the world's second-largest economy, would continue comprehensive economic reforms, he said, without elaborating.

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia cancelled the registration of the country's main opposition coalition  Perikatan Nasional (PN) on Tuesday (Oct 20) amid a dispute between its key parties, dealing a blow to the bloc  ahead of elections expected in coming months .  Malaysia's Melaka state is due to hold a vote on Nov 14, in the latest test for Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim following  defeats in two other regional polls earlier this year. An early general election could also be triggered amid simmering tensions within Anwar's multi-party ruling coalition.    But opposition group PN is facing growing rifts of its own between the conservative Islamist party  Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) - which has the most seats of any single party in Malaysia's 222-member parliament - and the Malay nationalist party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), with both vying for leadership of the coalition.  Bersatu, led by former prime minister Muhyiddin Yassin, had filed a complaint to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) alleging that it had been excluded from a PN supreme council meeting in July, describing it as a breach of the coalition's constitution by rival grouping PAS.  RoS said in a Tuesday statement that it had received an unsatisfactory response from PN after warning last month that the bloc could face de-registration. It said "the reasons given failed to refute the grounds for the cancellation of registration".  PN's dissolution would mean that its component parties, including several other smaller organisations aside from Bersatu and PAS, would not be able to contest the elections under a common banner. Despite contesting under the PN banner, Bersatu and PAS campaigned in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan state polls separately.

PN secretary-general Takiyuddin Hassan, who is also a PAS leader, said on Tuesday that the coalition would file a legal challenge against the de-registration order. "PN condemns this action as an attempt to ... weaken political opponents ahead of the Melaka election," Takiyuddin said in a statement.  He said the RoS issued its show-cause notice on Sep 22, the day the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly was announced, and suspended PN’s activities the following day, local news outlet Free Malaysia Today reported.  Political parties under the now deregistered coalition have yet to decide which logo to use for the upcoming Melaka state polls , The Star reported Takiyuddinas saying. Polling for the Melaka state election is scheduled for Nov 14, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10. Anwar leads a government consisting of several blocs, including his own Pakatan Harapan coalition as well as the Barisan Nasional (BN), led by the once-dominant United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), the party of jailed former premier Najib Razak.  Despite their federal partnership, Pakatan and Barisan remain rivals in some states, with the parties exploring different electoral strategies ahead of the next general election.  BN and PAS have said they are discussing cooperation in the Melaka polls, an arrangement that could test the prospects of a broader electoral alliance, according to local media reports.

Oct 20 : AstraZeneca said on Tuesday that it is working with Oracle to use AI and real-world data to identify eligible patients for clinical trials and monitor safety signals, among other measures, as the drugmaker looks to improve clinical research. • The collaboration will combine AstraZeneca's drug development expertise with Oracle's AI and healthcare data capabilities to support patient matching and research • Initial work will focus on cancer, cardiovascular, respiratory, immunology and rare diseases, and could also support earlier diagnosis of serious diseases • The first project will support hypertension research in Abu Dhabi in partnership with UAE-based healthcare firm M42
